title: Enlarging the marking inside its pi-zero closure preserves diagonal hammocks
statement:
Let $A$ be a small simplicial category, with object set $O$, mapping simplicial sets $A(x,y)$, associative unital simplicial composition, and category of components $\pi_0A$ [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $U\subseteq V\subseteq A$ be wide simplicial subcategories, meaning that they have object set $O$, contain every identity, and are closed under composition and simplicial operators. Use the diagonal reduced hammock categories of [def-coef-simplicial-hammock-pair]. Let $Q$ be the ordinary category obtained from $\pi_0A$ by formally adjoining inverses to the images of all vertices of $U$, imposing composition and inverse relations. Suppose the image in $Q$ of every vertex of $V$ is invertible. Then the canonical simplicial functor
$$\operatorname{diag}H(A,U)\longrightarrow\operatorname{diag}H(A,V),$$
which leaves every hammock arrow unchanged and reduces with the larger marking, induces a weak homotopy equivalence on each mapping simplicial set. No Kan, cofibrancy, model-category, two-out-of-three or saturation hypothesis is imposed on $A,U,V$.

source.place: Dwyer--Kan, Simplicial localizations of categories, Closure Lemma 6.4 and Corollary 6.5, printed p.276, with Proposition 10.5, pp.282-283; diagonal-hammock formulation via Calculating simplicial localizations, Remark 2.5, p.20 (dwyer-kan-2.pdf). Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this enriched localization result.
